title: Live GPS updates enable direct linkability of transmissions to the same child over time
description: Regular transmission of precise GPS coordinates from the child's device can allow an observer or recipient to link multiple messages to the same child, building a persistent movement history even if explicit identifiers are minimized.
assumptions: The flow is repeated over time and carries a stable device, account, session, or network identifier, or otherwise remains distinguishable across updates.
uncertainty_note: Tree node id is my best fit for linkability of repeated observations; exact LINDDUN Pro numbering may vary.

title: Precise location updates reveal the child's identity or enable singling out
description: Live GPS coordinates sent at regular intervals can identify the child directly or indirectly by revealing home, school, or habitual routes, allowing the backend or anyone with access to infer who the child is.
assumptions: The backend can associate coordinates with other customer, device, or contextual data, or the locations themselves are unique enough to identify the child.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort node id for identifiability from direct or quasi-identifying data; exact numbering may differ.

title: Continuous GPS collection enables detailed tracking and profiling of the child's movements
description: Regular live GPS uploads disclose extensive personal information, such as routines, visited places, school attendance, religious venues, medical visits, and social relationships, beyond what may be necessary for the service.
assumptions: Location data is stored, analyzed, or otherwise accessible beyond transient routing.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort node id for disclosure of sensitive personal information through data content and aggregation.

title: Collection frequency may exceed necessity and proportionality for the stated purpose
description: Sending live GPS coordinates at regular intervals may constitute excessive collection if the service purpose could be fulfilled with coarser granularity, lower frequency, or on-device processing, creating a data minimization risk.
assumptions: The exact business purpose is not provided and may not require continuous high-precision tracking.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort node id for data minimization / unnecessary detail or frequency; exact LINDDUN Pro node numbering may differ.

title: The child may not understand or meaningfully consent to continuous location transmission
description: Because the data subject is a child, regular backend transmission of live GPS data raises a privacy unawareness risk if explanations, indicators, parental controls, or age-appropriate notices are insufficient for the child to understand the collection and its consequences.
assumptions: The child is the primary user of the device or app and receives limited or no age-appropriate notice about ongoing tracking.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort node id for unawareness due to insufficient user understanding or notice; numbering may vary.

title: Continuous child-location tracking may violate consent and child-data protection requirements
description: Regular transmission of a child's precise GPS coordinates to the backend may be non-compliant with privacy obligations if valid consent, parental authorization, purpose limitation, retention limits, security safeguards, or other child-specific legal requirements are not satisfied.
assumptions: Applicable law or policy imposes heightened conditions for processing children's precise geolocation data.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort node id for non-compliance with legal/policy requirements; exact numbering may differ.

title: The child may be unable to later prove or challenge whether location data was sent
description: If transmission events are not made transparent and auditable to the child or guardian, they may be unable to repudiate, verify, or contest claims about when precise location data was uploaded, weakening accountability around sensitive tracking.
assumptions: There is no user-accessible log, receipt, or guardian-visible audit trail for location transmissions.
uncertainty_note: Repudiation is a weaker fit for this flow than other categories; included because auditability of sensitive child-location transmission can matter. Node id is approximate.

title: Backend can link repeated location pings to the same user/device over time
description: Because the backend writes each location ping into a history store, the stored records can be correlated by account ID, device ID, pseudonymous identifier, or other stable metadata. This enables construction of long-term movement profiles and linking of multiple events to the same individual.
assumptions: Assumes each ping is stored with a stable identifier or metadata that allows correlation across records.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id from memory; exact LINDDUN Pro node may differ.

title: Stored location history can reveal identity through direct or indirect identifiers
description: Location history entries may include direct identifiers or be easily tied back to a person through user account references, device identifiers, home/work patterns, or unique trajectories. Even if explicit names are absent, the datastore contents may permit identification of the data subject.
assumptions: Assumes the store contains or is linkable to identifiers, or trajectories are sufficiently unique to identify individuals.
uncertainty_note: Node id is a best-effort estimate; exact subtree for identifiability of stored data may vary.

title: Location history disclosure exposes sensitive movements and habits
description: If the location history store is accessed by unauthorized parties or over-broadly shared internally, highly sensitive information can be inferred, such as home and work locations, routines, visits to medical, religious, or political venues, and social relationships.
assumptions: Assumes unauthorized access, excessive internal access, or secondary use of the stored history is possible.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id from memory for information disclosure from stored data.

title: Continuous retention of granular location history enables detectability of a person's presence and behavior
description: A persistent history store containing each location ping makes it possible to detect whether a person was at a particular place or followed a certain route at a specific time. The mere existence of records increases the detectability of the individual's activities and presence.
assumptions: Assumes queries or analysis can be performed over retained history.
uncertainty_note: Tree node id is approximate; detectability subnode may differ in the official threat tree.

title: Backend may store location pings beyond user expectations or stated purpose
description: Users may expect location data to be used only transiently for an active service, while the backend writes every ping into a long-term history store. If the storage purpose, granularity, or retention period is not transparent, users may be unaware of how extensively their movements are recorded.
assumptions: Assumes users are not fully informed about persistent storage, retention, or downstream uses of location history.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort node selection for unawareness; exact node id may differ.

title: Persisting each location ping may be non-compliant with data minimization or purpose-limitation requirements
description: Writing every location ping to historical storage may exceed what is necessary for the service, especially if high-frequency, precise, or indefinite retention is not justified. This can create non-compliance risks related to lawful basis, proportionality, retention limitation, and use beyond the original purpose.
assumptions: Assumes applicable privacy obligations require minimization, purpose limitation, retention limits, and transparency.
uncertainty_note: Exact non-compliance subtree is uncertain; node id is a best-fit estimate.

title: Linkability of repeated location pings across time

uncertainty_note: Tree node id is my best estimate for linkability via repeated observations; exact LINDDUN Pro node naming may vary.

The backend therefore receives enough quasi-identifiers to single out a specific minor.

assumptions: Assumes network/application metadata, event logs, or backend-side observables distinguish this flow from ordinary app traffic.

uncertainty_note: Best-fit node for non-compliant collection/processing; exact LINDDUN Pro node id may differ by version.
